# INCIDB — The Skincare & Cosmetics INCI Database

> A normalised relational snapshot of cosmetic ingredient labels: 18,583 products, 5,925 brands, 46,008 distinct canonical INCI names, 342,208 ordered product→ingredient composition links, and a 77,257-row `ingredient_name_map` recording how every raw label token was resolved to a canonical name. Product/brand/composition data from Open Beauty Facts (ODbL); ingredient enrichment (functions, CAS, EC numbers, chemical descriptions, Annex II–VI membership, restrictions) joined on exact canonical name from the European Commission CosIng inventory. Where a source has no value the column is NULL — nothing is defaulted or inferred. Snapshot 2026.09.

## Measured Enrichment Coverage (do not round up)
Coverage is reported two ways, because they differ by an order of magnitude and only quoting one would mislead:
- **CosIng match:** 11.6% of the 46,008 distinct canonical names; 83.9% of the 342,208 ingredient occurrences on product labels (link-weighted).
- **`functions` (CosIng vocabulary, multi-valued):** 11.5% of distinct names; 82.9% link-weighted.
- **`cas_number`:** 8.7% of distinct names; 77.6% link-weighted.
- **`chemical_description`:** 9.0% of distinct names, 4,101 distinct values.
- **EU fragrance allergens (`is_common_allergen`, `fragrance_allergens`).** The 81 labelling entries of Annex III to Regulation (EC) 1223/2009, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/1545 (consolidated text of 18.05.2026), are matched to INCIDB by exact INCI name, then by the collective label name the Regulation prescribes (e.g. "Rose Ketones"), then by CAS number for chemically defined substances only. Botanical CAS hits are shipped as review rows, never flags. 121 names are flagged; 46.9% of products contain at least one. About 2.7% of products list ingredients as unsplit text that the allergen flags do not reach. The US FDA has not yet published its MoCRA fragrance-allergen list, so this dataset carries no US flag.
- **`regulatory_status`:** EU Annex II–VI status per ingredient and list entry (PROHIBITED / RESTRICTED / ALLOWED_WITH_CONDITIONS) from the European Commission CosIng exports, with product type, maximum concentration and conditions verbatim. Matched by the CosIng glossary name or the CosIng "Identified INGREDIENTS" name only; no CAS route. A row exists only where a list says something; absence of a row is not a status. Not legal advice.
- **`comedogenic_rating`:** 144 ingredients rated 0–5, transcribed from Fulton JE Jr., J Soc Cosmet Chem 1989;40:321–333 (Table I); NULL elsewhere.
- **`is_fungal_acne_trigger`:** 272 rule-derived flags (C11–C24 fatty acids and their esters, polysorbates 20/40/60/80, applied only to CosIng-matched ingredients). A heuristic, not a measured property. Basis: DOI 10.3389/fcimb.2020.00112, DOI 10.1093/femsyr/foaf043.

Reason for the gap between the two views: a real-world label corpus contains far more distinct strings (botanical variants, multilingual spellings, marketing tokens) than any regulatory inventory lists, but the ingredients that actually fill label slots are the ones CosIng covers.

## Capabilities & Specs
- **Tables:** `products`, `brands`, `ingredients`, `product_ingredients`, `ingredient_name_map`, `fragrance_allergens`, `regulatory_status`.
- **Formats:** pipe-delimited UTF-8 CSV (`|`) and Apache Parquet (`pyarrow`).
- **Canonicalisation:** raw label token → canonical INCI name via an explicit method recorded per row (`exact`, `cleaned`, `typo_map`, `percent_stripped`, `paren_stripped`, `synonym_map`, `slash_variant`, `split`, `slash_same_cas`, `unresolved_residual`, `unresolved`). Tokens no method resolves are re-split by explicit rules, never fuzzily; `part_index` and `split_rule` record each cut. The map ships with the data so every decision is auditable.
- **Sources:** Open Beauty Facts (product corpus, ODbL), European Commission CosIng (ingredient enrichment and the Annex II–VI exports, EU open data) and EUR-Lex (the consolidated Annex III text, © European Union).
- **Attribution:** "Product data © Open Beauty Facts contributors", licensed ODbL v1.0 (attribution + share-alike). "Contains data from the European Commission CosIng database."
- **Free sample:** 200 products with their brands, 1,106 referenced ingredients, their composition links and name-map rows. The draw is a seeded uniform random sample of the products whose ingredient lists are at least 80% CosIng-matched, so it reads better than the corpus average — plan against the corpus figures above.
- **Product:** INCIDB Complete — $79 one-time, all 7 tables in both formats plus the build report, instant Stripe checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/3cIfZi5t6fzwazV1E43840g
- **What the price buys:** the normalisation, canonicalisation, joining and measurement, plus hosted instant delivery. Not exclusive rights to the underlying data, which remains ODbL.
